Subject: Acme - Integration & Prompt Governance follow-up

Hi Dana —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and the action items we promised: 

1) Recap from discovery
- Primary use case: product search + contextual assistant inside Acme Console (supporting structured tool calls and reranking for search results).
- Traffic profile: ~400 QPS peak across US, latency target p50 < 120ms token generation.

2) Integration & architecture questions (we flagged these for the SRE/engineering team):
- SDK setup: preferred path is our hosted REST SDK (JS/Python). Any blocker for using SDK vs direct HTTP?
- Auth: you mentioned SSO + service accounts. We support API keys and OAuth2 with short-lived tokens; we can integrate with your IdP. Any compliance constraints (no long-lived keys)?
- Routing: you asked about region pinning for EU/US traffic — we can pin by customer + route fallback rules. Need to know if you require strict geo residency.
- Structured output & tool calling: we support JSON-schema enforced outputs and programmatic tool-calls (function calling). Do you have an existing tool-call contract?
- Embeddings & reranker: recommended flow is hybrid — embeddings for recall + a lightweight reranker model for relevance. Any constraints on vector storage?

3) Prompt governance / red team / versioning
- You asked about system prompt versioning, mitigations for prompt injection, and a red-team cadence. We have linchpin controls (immutable system prompt versions, prompt fingerprinting, and an evaluation harness we can run).

Next steps I propose: 
- Technical deep-dive with Dev Patel to walk SDK/auth/routing + sample code (30–45m).
- Share our SDK quickstart and a mutual action plan.
- Schedule a short red-team tabletop to surface prompt-injection risks and confirm remediation acceptance criteria.

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf, mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx

If those items look right, I can send a calendar invite for the deep-dive later this week.

Thanks —

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- SDK: JS SDK is preferred; our product engineers prefer SDKs for automatic retry/backoff and streaming support. No blockers there.
- Auth: we require enterprise SSO + short-lived service tokens (max 24h). Long-lived API keys are discouraged by our security team.
- Routing/residency: all production customer PII must remain in US regions for now; failover to non-US is only allowed for DR with approval.
- Tool calling: we have an internal tool API for product actions; we can share a proto/contract for the most common calls.
- Embeddings: we need a managed vector store that supports encryption-at-rest and deletion on demand.

Prompt governance: we absolutely want versioning and a red-team exercise. Also need to see your SOC2 and a short note on prompt-injection mitigations.

Can we do the technical deep-dive Thu 2026-03-04 11:00 PT? Rajiv and one of our infra engineers will join.

—Dana
Dana Lee
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp

Hi Dana / Rajiv —

I’ll run the tech deep-dive. Quick notes ahead of the call so you have something to review: 

1) SDK setup & auth- JS SDK supports both browser and Node (recommended internal wrapper for streams). We authenticate using short-lived OAuth tokens (works with most IdPs). For service-to-service we issue ephemeral tokens via our control plane; token TTLs are configurable down to minutes. 

Sample snippet (Node):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ token: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN });
const resp = await client.chat.generate({ model: 'redwood-large-v1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: '...'}], stream: true });

2) Routing & residency- We support customer-level region pinning and per-request region overrides. Failover policies support DR to an alternate region but we can require manual approval for cross-border failover.

3) Structured output / tool calling- We enforce JSON schema on responses when you provide a schema; we also support typed tool/function calling with explicit argument validation and fallback handlers. Typical pattern:
- Provide a system prompt + tool definitions
- Use response schema validation, log mismatches, and optionally auto-retry with a different prompt template

4) Embeddings & rerank- Recommended flow:
- Generate dense embeddings for documents (we support batched embedding creation and streaming inserts to your vector DB).
- Store in encrypted vector store (our managed option or your own).
- For retrieval we do a candidate recall via embeddings then run an MLP or small reranker model hosted as a fast endpoint to rescore top-K.

5) Prompt governance / injection mitigations- Controls we offer: 
- Immutable system-prompt versions with an assigned semantic version and changelog (e.g., v1.2.0).
- Prompt fingerprinting: we compute a hash for every user prompt and keep exposure logs to detect suspicious prompt injection patterns.
- Response schema enforcement (deny outputs that don't match expected JSON).
- Red-team harness: we can run a set of adversarial prompts against your integration and produce a categorized findings report.

Attachments: sdk-quickstart.md (contains code samples, install steps, and config for region pinning).

Prep for Thu 11:00 PT: please share a sample tool contract (proto or OpenAPI) and a small example dataset for embeddings so we can estimate costs and throughput.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
